The challenge returned no_close_match_in_this_search and flagged an unrelated pharmacy paper on the design element 'frozen pretrained encoder'; Sachan et al., Mukherjee et al. and Lebmeier et al. were found by web search.

papers.title: Does syntax matter? A strong baseline for Aspect-based Sentiment Analysis with RoBERTa
papers.venue: Proceedings of the 2021 Conference of the North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies
papers.method: Compares parser trees, PTM-induced trees, FT-PTM-induced trees and left/right-chain trees inside ASGCN, PWCN and RGAT; RoBERTa with an MLP head as baseline
papers.datasets: Rest14, Laptop14, Twitter; three SemEval-2016 non-English sets
papers.findings: Full text: tree-structure comparison uses GloVe embeddings, 3 runs. SOTA table: RoBERTa-MLP 87.37/83.78 accuracy (Rest14/Laptop14) vs RoBERTa+ASGCN, PWCN, RGAT with parser or FT-RoBERTa trees between 86.87 and 87.52 (Rest14) and 81.66-84.16 (Laptop14); text: 'incorporating trees over the RoBERTa brings no significant improvement'. No variance reported for that table.
papers.limitations: Code (README): released logs are single runs; finetune.py uses the test set as dev for model selection; released tree-model code uses GloVe only, so the RoBERTa+tree rows cannot be re-run from the repository; no licence

papers.title: Do Syntax Trees Help Pre-trained Transformers Extract Information?

sections.summary: The question as posed is already answered: Dai et al. ran RoBERTa with and without ASGCN, PWCN and RGAT tree heads on the same SemEval data and found no significant gain [@dai2021syntax]. What remains open is whether that null result, and the 2023-2026 claims of gains, survive a sound protocol: the closest codebases select models on the test set, a selection habit worth 1-2 points elsewhere in ABSA [@mukherjee2021repro], about the size of every claimed syntax gain. A protocol-corrected replication with structure controls is a conditional go; a novel framing (frozen vs fine-tuned encoder) is plausible but unverified.

well_explored.text: New dependency-GCN architectures on SemEval-2014 (many 2022-2026 papers; titles screened)
On Rest14 and Laptop14, RoBERTa+tree heads lie within about +/-1.1 (Rest14) and -2.1 to +0.4 (Laptop14) accuracy points of RoBERTa-MLP, with no variance reported.
Whether syntax helps fine-tuned transformers on information extraction
Reproducibility of ABSA results in general

recommendation.text: No-go for the question as stated, and for the parser-quality variant.

Conditional go for D1 followed by D2 as one 6-8 week project: replicate the RoBERTa tree-head comparison with validation-based selection and 10+ seeds, then add chain, random and fully connected graph controls with matched parameters.
First action, no compute: read Lebmeier et al. through the library and screen ablation tables of the most cited 2022-2026 syntax-GCN papers for structure controls.
D3 (frozen encoder) is the only design with a novel framing; check the probing literature first.

opportunities.title: As stated: do syntax-tree GCNs help when the pretrained encoder is held fixed?
opportunities.revision_note: Already performed: Dai et al. compare RoBERTa-MLP with RoBERTa+ASGCN/PWCN/RGAT using parser and induced trees and conclude that trees bring no significant improvement [@dai2021syntax]; BERT4GCN's own ablation finds the dependency graph adds only slightly [@xiao2021bert4gcn]; and the same comparison under identical encoders is done in information extraction [@sachan2021syntax].
opportunities.research_question: With the encoder fixed, do dependency-tree GCN heads improve ABSA accuracy?

closest_existing_work.how_it_differs: Same encoder, with and without tree heads, same datasets; lacks variance and a validation split.
Ablates the dependency graph inside one architecture.
Same with/without-syntax design on SRL, NER and RE.

novelty.uncertainty: Answered in the full texts read.

opportunities.title: D1 (replication): protocol-corrected re-test of Dai et al.'s RoBERTa tree-head comparison
opportunities.revision_note: Narrowed from the original question after the full texts showed the comparison exists but was run with test-set model selection, without variance and without released code for the RoBERTa+tree rows.
opportunities.research_question: On the shipped SemEval-2014 Laptop and Restaurant splits, does the reported null result (no gain from tree heads on RoBERTa) survive validation-based model selection, a tuned baseline and 10+ seeds, and does it hold for DeBERTa-v3-base?
opportunities.motivation: The headline null result is cited as settled but rests on test-selected, single-table numbers [@dai2021syntax].

closest_existing_work.how_it_differs: The study being replicated; the replication changes the protocol, not the question.
Re-runs six transformer ABSA architectures with validation splits and uncertainty; whether any is a syntax-GCN model is unknown.
Quantifies test-selection inflation, but for memory-network and BERT models, not tree heads.

gap_evidence.text: On Rest14 and Laptop14, RoBERTa+tree heads lie within about +/-1.1 (Rest14) and -2.1 to +0.4 (Laptop14) accuracy points of RoBERTa-MLP, with no variance reported.

Official code of the closest studies selects on the test set: RoBERTaABSA finetune.py passes the test split as dev_data and reloads the best model; ASGCN (original and Dai et al.'s copy) keeps max_test_acc and max_test_f1 separately, so accuracy and F1 can come from different epochs; RGAT run.py reports the best evaluation on the test set.
Selecting on a 15% held-out split instead of the test set costs a further 1-2 accuracy points for six non-syntax ABSA models, about the size of the claimed syntax gains.
The same RoBERTa-MLP baseline is reported at 83.78 (Dai et al.) and 81.11 (BERT4GCN) on Laptop14, so cross-paper syntax gains can be baseline artefacts.

opportunities.contribution: A checked, variance-aware answer to a question the field treats as settled; either outcome is reportable.

novelty.uncertainty: Replication value, not novelty. Lebmeier et al.'s architectures are unknown; a paywalled or non-English replication could exist.

feasibility.text: Shipped splits and pre-parsed dependency trees (head, deprel fields) are in the RoBERTaABSA repository; RoBERTa-base and DeBERTa-v3-base are MIT-licensed on Hugging Face.
About 3,600 training aspects; base encoders at batch 16 fit 8 GB with mixed precision; roughly 2 datasets x 2 encoders x 3 heads x 10 seeds = 120 short runs, about 15-30 GPU-hours.
Tree heads must be reimplemented on current transformers (repository pins transformers 2.11, PyTorch 1.5, fastNLP).

evidence.text: Official code of the closest studies selects on the test set: RoBERTaABSA finetune.py passes the test split as dev_data and reloads the best model; ASGCN (original and Dai et al.'s copy) keeps max_test_acc and max_test_f1 separately, so accuracy and F1 can come from different epochs; RGAT run.py reports the best evaluation on the test set.

methodological_risks.mitigation: Validation split carved from training, grouped by sentence; select checkpoints and hyperparameters on it only; touch the test set once.

evidence.text: ASGCN reports maximum accuracy and maximum F1 from possibly different epochs.

methodological_risks.mitigation: Report accuracy and macro-F1 of one selected checkpoint.

evidence.text: Dai et al.: 3 runs for the tree comparison, no variance for the RoBERTa table, released logs single-run; Lebmeier et al. report notable variance across data splits.

methodological_risks.mitigation: At least 10 seeds x repeated train/validation splits; paired comparisons; confidence intervals.

evidence.text: The same RoBERTa-MLP baseline is reported at 83.78 (Dai et al.) and 81.11 (BERT4GCN) on Laptop14, so cross-paper syntax gains can be baseline artefacts.

methodological_risks.mitigation: Tune the plain-encoder baseline with the same budget and search space as the tree heads.

evidence.text: No public code for the RoBERTa+tree rows; the Hugging Face SetFit copy has 654 laptop test rows vs 638 aspects in the shipped split.

methodological_risks.mitigation: Use the shipped split files; reimplement heads on one codebase; label the work a replication.

methodological_risks.evidence: Tree heads add parameters and a separate learning rate; Dai et al. note RoBERTa-based tree models are hard to optimise and need different learning rates.
methodological_risks.mitigation: Parameter-matched no-graph head with the same tuning budget.

evidence.text: Shipped splits (Laptop 2328/638, Restaurants 3608/1120 aspects, matching Dai et al.'s statistics): one exact duplicate sentence per dataset, same label; an aspect-term vote reaches 52.5% vs majority 53.4% (Laptop) and 65.4% vs 65.0% (Restaurants), so no aspect-identity shortcut.

Shipped splits (Laptop 2328/638, Restaurants 3608/1120 aspects, matching Dai et al.'s statistics): one exact duplicate sentence per dataset, same label; an aspect-term vote reaches 52.5% vs majority 53.4% (Laptop) and 65.4% vs 65.0% (Restaurants), so no aspect-identity shortcut.

methodological_risks.evidence: SemEval-2014 reviews have been public since 2014 and may be in RoBERTa/DeBERTa pre-training data; this affects both arms of a with/without-syntax comparison alike.

decision.rationale: Feasible and useful as a replication; novelty is low by design.
conditions: Read Lebmeier et al. through the library; if it already re-runs a syntax-GCN model with validation splits and uncertainty, narrow to the DeBERTa-v3 part or drop D1.
Fix the validation protocol, seeds and the smallest effect of interest (e.g. 1 point) before any run.
unresolved_risks: Reimplementation may not match Dai et al.'s unreleased RoBERTa+tree code

opportunities.title: D2 (extension): is it syntax, or just an extra graph head? Structure controls on a fixed fine-tuned encoder
opportunities.research_question: With the encoder and head parameter count fixed, do dependency trees beat left/right-chain, degree-matched random trees and a fully connected graph inside the same GCN head?
opportunities.motivation: Dai et al. ran chain-tree controls only with GloVe models [@dai2021syntax]; random masks also help in Syntax-BERT [@bai2021syntaxbert]; BERT4GCN's graph adds only slightly [@xiao2021bert4gcn].

closest_existing_work.how_it_differs: Chain-tree controls with GloVe embeddings only, 3 runs.
Random-mask control inside the transformer, GLUE tasks, not ABSA.
Removes the dependency graph but has no random or chain-tree control.
Unknown architectures; unlikely to include structure controls.

gap_evidence.text: Chain-tree controls in Dai et al. use 300-d GloVe embeddings kept fixed, not a pretrained encoder.
A random decomposition of the network also gives moderate improvements (Syntax-BERT, GLUE).

opportunities.contribution: Separates the effect of syntax from that of adding any graph-structured head.

novelty.uncertainty: No ABSA paper with random/chain-tree controls on a pretrained encoder was found in the full texts read or by web search; ablation tables of the many 2022-2026 GCN papers were not all read and may contain such controls.

opportunities.title: D3 (novel investigation): frozen versus fine-tuned encoder - does syntax matter only when the encoder cannot adapt?
opportunities.research_question: When the encoder is frozen (features only), do dependency-tree heads give larger gains over a parameter-matched no-graph head than when it is fine-tuned?
opportunities.motivation: Every closest study fine-tunes the encoder [@dai2021syntax; @sachan2021syntax]; Dai et al. argue fine-tuning makes the encoder learn task-oriented structure implicitly.

closest_existing_work.how_it_differs: Fine-tuned encoders only, information extraction tasks.
Fine-tuned RoBERTa only; frozen GloVe for the tree comparison.
BERT + GCN depth variants; encoder regime not read.

gap_evidence.text: The closest full texts fine-tune the encoder in every syntax comparison.
If fine-tuning lets the encoder absorb task structure, a frozen encoder should leave more room for explicit syntax.

opportunities.contribution: Identifies when explicit syntax is worth adding (compute-limited, frozen-feature settings).

novelty.uncertainty: Unverified hypothesis: probing and adapter literature with frozen encoders was not searched in depth.

datasets.format: JSON with tokens, POS, dependency heads and relations; original XML

datasets.name: SemEval-2014 restaurants (SetFit copy)
datasets.suitability: Row counts differ from the published split (laptop copy: 654 test rows vs 638 aspects)

limitations: Lebmeier et al. (2023) was not read beyond its abstract; it may already contain part of D1.
The ablation tables of most 2022-2026 syntax-GCN ABSA papers were not read; D2's controls may exist there.
Semantic Scholar was rate-limited; the challenge command did not retrieve three of the closest papers, which were found by web search.
Compute and time figures are estimates; no model was trained and no code was run beyond data checks.
SemEval-2014 data licence is not stated on any copy checked.
